correctness.rationale: Every n>=2 and 0<r<1/2 is covered. The isolation event leaves an independent uniform complement arc of length q=1-2r; the circular edge test reduces to ordinary arc separation because crossing the excluded arc costs at least 2r. The exact pair integral gives h=1-((q-r)_+/q)^2, and combinatorial double counting gives the covariance. Sign reduction produces a quadratic for r<=1/3 and a linear form for r>=1/3; discriminants and root positions prove all cases. Sparse limit follows from r=lambda/n expansion. The extracted stdlib checker independently verifies 588 exact and grid-limit identities; finite grid observations are not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Edge count and isolates are standard density/connectivity indicators; their mixed dependence in a fixed-size circular geometric graph is not determined by marginal models. Conditioning on one isolate both removes its incident edges and clusters other vertices into a residual arc. This competition produces a sharp all-n two-crossing phase diagram, minimum order six and sparse critical scale nr=4/3. The result is structural, motivated, and applies to infinitely many n rather than being a one-off numerical example.
